name: Standard Application Layer Protocol
summary: Adversaries may establish command and control capabilities over commonly used application layer protocols such as HTTP(S), OPC, RDP, telnet, DNP3, and modbus. These protocols may be used to disguise adversary actions as benign network traffic. Standard protocols may be seen on their associated port or in some cases over a non-standard port. strategies.name: Detection of Standard Application Layer Protocol

analytics.name: Analytic 1931
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies Domain Name System (DNS) queries from Industrial Control System (ICS) host Internet Protocol (IP) addresses to external resolvers for domains not associated with any approved ICS vendor, particularly domains exhibiting Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA)-like patterns. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the asset's documented role does not permit the connection and the destination/proxy/service is outside the approved communications profile, with process/service identity used as corroboration where available. Suppress approved vendor support, update repositories, remote operations, failover paths, and documented temporary connectivity.

analytics.name: Analytic 2155
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux service processes initiating outbound application-layer protocol connections to ports/destinations outside the approved communication matrix. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the asset's documented role does not permit the connection and the destination/proxy/service is outside the approved communications profile, with process/service identity used as corroboration where available. Suppress approved vendor support, update repositories, remote operations, failover paths, and documented temporary connectivity.
